create_tts.title: Create text-to-speech task (deprecated)
create_tts.description: Start an asynchronous text-to-speech task for `text` in a given voice and language. Returns a task_id; poll get_tts_status, then fetch the audio with get_tts_result (pass output_type=file_url for a download link). CAMB.AI marks this endpoint deprecated in favour of stream_tts, but it is the only TTS path that yields a URL rather than raw audio bytes.
create_tts.notes: Deprecated by CAMB.AI; still documented and served.

project_name.description: Enter a distinctive name for your project that reflects its purpose or content. This name will be displayed in your CAMB.AI workspace dashboard and used to organize related assets, transcriptions, etc.. . Choose something memorable that helps you quickly identify this specific project among your other voice, audio and localization tasks.

project_description.description: Provide details about your project's goals and specifications. Include information such as the target languages for translation or dubbing, desired voice characteristics, emotional tones to capture, or specific audio processing requirements, outlining the workflow here can serve as valuable documentation for organizational purposes.

text.description: The text to be converted to speech

voice_id.description: The voice ID to be used to generate speech.

language.description: The language of the input text. Pass a locale tag (`en-us`, `fr-fr`, `es-es`). Numeric language IDs (`1` or `"1"`) still work but are deprecated. (see list_source_languages).

gender.description: Speaker gender code: 0 not specified, 1 male, 2 female, 9 neutral.

age.description: The age of the speaker in the generated speech.

output.description: The new text-to-speech task; poll its `task_id` with the matching status tool.

task_id.description: Id to poll for status.

get_tts_status.title: Get text-to-speech task status
get_tts_status.description: Check the status of a text-to-speech task created with create_tts. Poll until `status` is SUCCESS (keep polling while PENDING; ERROR, TIMEOUT and PAYMENT_REQUIRED are terminal), then use the returned `run_id` with get_tts_result.

task_id.description: A unique identifier for the task. This is used to query the status of the text to speech task that is running. It is returned when a create request is made for a text to speech.

output.description: Task status: `status` is PENDING, SUCCESS, ERROR, TIMEOUT or PAYMENT_REQUIRED; `run_id` is set once it succeeds.

status.description: PENDING, SUCCESS, ERROR, TIMEOUT or PAYMENT_REQUIRED.

run_id.description: The run holding the result, once status is SUCCESS.

get_tts_result.title: Get text-to-speech result
get_tts_result.description: Fetch the result of a finished text-to-speech run. With output_type=file_url (the default here) it returns JSON holding a URL to the generated audio file; raw_bytes streams the FLAC audio itself, which is not useful as text.
get_tts_result.notes: CAMB.AI's own default is raw_bytes; this tool defaults to file_url so the result is a usable link.

run_id.description: The unique identifier for the run, which was generated during the Text-to-Speech creation process and returned upon task completion.

output_type.description: The type of the Text-to-Speech output to return. Either streamable audio bytes or a URL to the generated file.

output.description: With file_url, an object with the audio file URL; with raw_bytes, the audio bytes.

get_tts_results_bulk.title: Get text-to-speech results in bulk
get_tts_results_bulk.description: Fetch the results of several text-to-speech runs at once. Takes 2 to 5 run ids of the same run type and returns their results keyed by run id. Use get_tts_result for a single run.

run_ids.description: An array of unique positive integers, each representing the ID of a specific run. You must provide between 2 and 5 IDs, and all IDs must correspond to the same run type (e.g., all text-to-speech or all dubbing runs).

stream_tts.title: Stream text-to-speech audio
stream_tts.description: Synthesize speech from text (3-3000 characters) and return the audio bytes directly in the chosen format, with model, voice settings and output configuration. The response body is binary audio, not JSON; to get a downloadable URL instead use create_tts and get_tts_result. Pick voice_id from list_voices.

text.description: The text to synthesize into speech (3–3000 characters). For `mars-8.1-flash-beta` and `mars-8.1-pro-beta`, you can include inline controls such as CMU phonemes (`[B EY1 S]`) and non-verbal tags (`[laughter]`).

language.description: The language of the input text. Pass a locale tag (`en-us`, `fr-fr`, `es-es`). Numeric language IDs (`1` or `"1"`) still work but are deprecated. (see list_source_languages).

voice_id.description: Voice profile ID to use for synthesis. Get available IDs from `/list-voices`.

speech_model.description: Speech model variant to use for synthesis. Use `mars-8.1-flash-beta` or `mars-8.1-pro-beta` to leverage inline pronunciation and non-verbal controls in `text`.

enhance_named_entities_pronunciation.description: If `true`, improves pronunciation of names, brands, and other named entities.

output_configuration.description: Controls output format and enhancement options for the stream.

format.description: Audio format for the streamed response. Choose a container (`mp3`, `wav`, `flac`, `adts`) or a raw PCM format (`pcm_*`).

sample_rate.description: Optional sample rate in Hz. Use this to control the audio quality and compatibility with different devices.

apply_enhancement.description: If `true`, applies output audio enhancement (loudness, denoising, polish). Defaults to `true` for most models; `false` for the speed-oriented `mars-flash` and `mars-8.1-flash-beta` models. Set explici

voice_settings.description: Voice behavior preferences such as accent preservation and reference enhancement.

enhance_reference_audio_quality.description: Remove noise from reference audio. (useful when the reference has background noise or compression).

maintain_source_accent.description: Maintain the accent from the original source audio.

speaking_rate.description: Controls playback speed for generated speech.

output.description: The synthesized audio bytes in the requested format (binary, not JSON).

gender.description: Gender of the synthesized voice: 0 not specified, 1 male (default), 2 female, 9 neutral.

create_dubbing.title: Create end-to-end dubbing task
create_dubbing.description: Start an end-to-end dubbing task for a video or audio URL: transcribe, translate and re-voice into the target languages, optionally from SRTs you supply. Returns a task_id; poll get_dubbing_status, then use get_dubbing_result. Use create_project_setup instead to prepare a project for editing in CAMB.AI Studio.

source_transcript.description: Optional original-language SRT contents. Send the file text in JSON, not a file path or URL.

content.description: SRT file contents, limited to 2 MiB encoded as UTF-8. Must contain at least one cue parsed by the srt library with parse errors enabled. No additional cue-count, numbering, timing, ordering, control-c

target_transcripts.description: Optional translated SRTs, one per requested target language. Languages must be unique after normalization. Source and target SRT contents must not exceed 10 MiB UTF-8 combined.

video_url.description: The URL of the media file to be used to create the end-to-end dubbing task.

source_language.description: The language of the input text. Pass a locale tag (`en-us`, `fr-fr`, `es-es`). Numeric language IDs (`1` or `"1"`) still work but are deprecated. (see list_source_languages).

target_languages.description: Languages to generate output in. Pass locale tags (`es-es`, `fr-fr`, `de-de`). Numeric language IDs still work but are deprecated. (see list_target_languages).

project_description.description: Provide details about your project's goals and specifications. selected_audio_tracks.description: Optional array of one or two zero‑based audio track indices to dub. Only supported for `MXF` files. If omitted, the first audio track (index 0) is used by default.

add_output_as_an_audio_track.description: Optional flag to append the dubbed audio as a new audio track in the output file. Only supported for `MXF` files. If `true`, the dubbed audio is added as an additional track; if `false` or omitted, the source would be returned with only dubbed audio.

chosen_dictionaries.description: An optional list of dictionary IDs selected by the user. Each entry must be an integer corresponding to a valid dictionary ID. If provided, at least one ID is required.

target_language.description: The target output language. Pass a locale tag (`fr-fr`, `es-es`, `de-de`). Numeric language IDs still work but are deprecated. (see list_target_languages).

transcription_mode.description: Transcription mode. `fast` (default) is quicker; `slow` takes longer and may produce a more accurate transcript.

include_music_in_fg.description: Keep music in the foreground audio during source separation. When `true` (default), background music is preserved alongside speech; set to `false` to strip music out of the foreground.

language.description: Source audio language: a locale such as en-us, a numeric language ID, or auto for automatic detection (also accepted as ax-ax or 321).

media_url.description: Public URL of the video or audio file to transcribe.

transcription_mode.description: fast (default) prioritizes speed; slow takes longer and may improve accuracy. Both modes include speaker diarization. Independent of run_audio_cleaning.

include_music_in_fg.description: Keep music in foreground audio during source separation (default true). Set false to remove music from the foreground. Has no effect when run_audio_cleaning is false.

formatting_options.description: Optional JSON-encoded string of subtitle formatting rules (segmentation runs in the source language). Keys: max_segment_duration_in_seconds, min_segment_duration_in_seconds, max_characters_in_segment, max_reading_speed_in_cps, min_gap_between_segments_in_frames.

run_audio_cleaning.description: Run source separation before transcription. Set false for clean speech to skip separation. Media extraction, decoding and transcription preparation still run, including when formatting_options is supplied. This does not disable diarization.

output.description: The new transcription task; poll its `task_id` with the matching status tool.

task_id.description: Id to poll for status.

get_transcription_status.title: Get transcription status
get_transcription_status.description: Check the status of a transcription task. Poll until `status` is SUCCESS (keep polling while PENDING; ERROR, TIMEOUT and PAYMENT_REQUIRED are terminal), then use the returned `run_id` with get_transcription_result.

task_id.description: A unique identifier for the task. This is used to query the status of the transcription task that is running. It is returned when a create request is made for transcription.

output.description: Task status: `status` is PENDING, SUCCESS, ERROR, TIMEOUT or PAYMENT_REQUIRED; `run_id` is set once it succeeds.

status.description: PENDING, SUCCESS, ERROR, TIMEOUT or PAYMENT_REQUIRED.

run_id.description: The run holding the result, once status is SUCCESS.

get_transcription_result.title: Get transcription result
get_transcription_result.description: Get the transcript of a finished transcription run: structured JSON segments (start, end, text, speaker) by default, or an srt/vtt/txt export as raw text or a presigned URL when format_type/data_type are set.

run_id.description: The unique identifier for the run, which was generated during the transcription creation process and returned upon task completion.

format_type.description: Subtitle format for the transcript export: `srt`, `vtt` or `txt`. When omitted (and `data_type` is also omitted) the structured JSON transcript is returned instead of an exported file.

data_type.description: How the exported transcript is returned once `format_type`/`data_type` is set: `file` returns a presigned URL, `raw_data` returns the raw text. Same values and response shape as the dubbing `/transcript` endpoint. In export mode the effective defaults are `format_type=txt`, `data_type=file`.

get_transcription_results_bulk.title: Get transcription results in bulk
get_transcription_results_bulk.description: Fetch the transcripts of several transcription runs at once. Takes 2 to 5 run ids of the same run type and returns their results keyed by run id.

run_ids.description: An array of unique positive integers, each representing the ID of a specific run. You must provide between 2 and 5 IDs, and all IDs must correspond to the same run type (e.g., all text-to-speech or all dubbing runs).

create_subtitles.title: Create subtitles
create_subtitles.description: Generate subtitle-ready segments for a media URL in the source language and one or more target languages, with optional formatting rules. Returns a task_id; poll get_subtitle_status, then get_subtitle_result or get_subtitle_result_for_language.

media_url.description: Public or signed URL to the media file for subtitle generation. Supports both video and audio files.

source_language.description: The language spoken in the source media. Pass a locale tag (`en-us`, `fr-fr`, `es-es`). Numeric language IDs still work but are deprecated. (see list_source_languages).

target_languages.description: One or more target languages for the subtitles. Pass locale tags (`es-es`, `fr-fr`, `de-de`), including a single-item array when you only need one language. Numeric language IDs still work but are deprecated. (see list_target_languages).

transcription_mode.description: Transcription mode. `fast` (default) is quicker; `slow` takes longer and may produce a more accurate transcript.

formatting_options.description: Optional subtitle formatting rules as a JSON object. When provided, subtitle segmentation runs for every target language. Omit to skip segmentation.

max_segment_duration_in_seconds.description: The longest a single cue may stay on screen.

min_segment_duration_in_seconds.description: The shortest a single cue may stay on screen.

max_characters_in_segment.description: The maximum number of characters allowed in one cue.

project_name.description: Enter a distinctive name for your project that reflects its purpose or content. This name will be displayed in your CAMB.AI workspace dashboard and used to organize related assets, transcriptions, etc.. . Choose something memorable that helps you quickly identify this specific project among your other voice, audio and localization tasks.

project_description.description: Provide details about your project's goals and specifications. Include information such as the target languages for translation or dubbing, desired voice characteristics, emotional tones to capture, or specific audio processing requirements, outlining the workflow here can serve as valuable documentation for organizational purposes.

folder_id.description: Optional folder ID to place the run in your workspace.

output.description: The new subtitle task; poll its `task_id` with the matching status tool.

task_id.description: Id to poll for status.

get_subtitle_status.title: Get subtitle task status
get_subtitle_status.description: Check the status of a subtitle task. Poll until `status` is SUCCESS (keep polling while PENDING; ERROR, TIMEOUT and PAYMENT_REQUIRED are terminal), then use the returned `run_id` with get_subtitle_result.

task_id.description: A unique identifier for the task. This is used to query the status of the subtitle task that is running. It is returned when a create request is made for subtitle generation.

output.description: Task status: `status` is PENDING, SUCCESS, ERROR, TIMEOUT or PAYMENT_REQUIRED; `run_id` is set once it succeeds.

status.description: PENDING, SUCCESS, ERROR, TIMEOUT or PAYMENT_REQUIRED.

run_id.description: The run holding the result, once status is SUCCESS.

get_subtitle_result.title: Get subtitle result
get_subtitle_result.description: Get the subtitles of a finished run for every language on it: structured JSON by default (keyed by language id when there are several), or srt/vtt/txt exports when format_type/data_type are set. Use get_subtitle_result_for_language for one language.

run_id.description: The unique identifier for the run, which was generated during the subtitle creation process and returned upon task completion.

format_type.description: Subtitle format for the transcript export: `srt`, `vtt` or `txt`. When omitted (and `data_type` is also omitted) the structured JSON transcript is returned instead of an exported file. Applies to every language on the run.

data_type.description: How the exported transcript is returned once `format_type`/`data_type` is set: `file` returns a presigned URL, `raw_data` returns the raw text. Same values as the dubbing `/transcript` and transcription-result endpoints. In export mode the effective defaults are `format_type=txt`, `data_type=file`. Applies to every language on the run.

get_subtitle_result_for_language.title: Get subtitle result for a language
get_subtitle_result_for_language.description: Get the subtitles of a finished run in a single language (the source or one of its targets), as structured JSON or an srt/vtt/txt export.

run_id.description: The unique identifier for the run, which was generated during the subtitle creation process and returned upon task completion.

language.description: The language to fetch, either the run's source language or one of its target languages. Pass a locale tag (`en-us`, `fr-fr`, `es-es`). Numeric language IDs still work but are deprecated. (see list_source_languages).

format_type.description: Subtitle format for the transcript export: `srt`, `vtt` or `txt`. When omitted (and `data_type` is also omitted) the structured JSON transcript is returned instead of an exported file.

data_type.description: How the exported transcript is returned once `format_type`/`data_type` is set: `file` returns a presigned URL, `raw_data` returns the raw text. Same values and response shape as the dubbing `/transcript` endpoint. In export mode the effective defaults are `format_type=txt`, `data_type=file`.

get_subtitle_results_bulk.title: Get subtitle results in bulk
get_subtitle_results_bulk.description: Fetch the subtitles of several subtitle runs at once, optionally exported to srt/vtt/txt. Takes 2 to 5 run ids of the same run type and returns their results keyed by run id.

format_type.description: Subtitle format for the transcript export: `srt`, `vtt` or `txt`. When omitted (and `data_type` is also omitted) the structured JSON transcript is returned instead of an exported file. Applied to every language on each run.

data_type.description: How the exported transcript is returned once `format_type`/`data_type` is set: `file` returns a presigned URL, `raw_data` returns the raw text. In export mode the effective defaults are `format_type=txt`, `data_type=file`. Applied to every language on each run.

run_ids.description: An array of unique positive integers, each representing the ID of a specific run. You must provide between 2 and 5 IDs, and all IDs must correspond to the same run type (e.g., all text-to-speech or all dubbing runs).

create_translation.title: Create translation
create_translation.description: Translate one or more text segments from source_language to target_language, with optional formality, grammatical gender, audience age and terminology dictionaries. Returns a task_id; poll get_translation_status, then get_translation_result.

project_name.description: Enter a distinctive name for your project that reflects its purpose or content. This name will be displayed in your CAMB.AI workspace dashboard and used to organize related assets, transcriptions, etc.. . Choose something memorable that helps you quickly identify this specific project among your other voice, audio and localization tasks.

project_description.description: Provide details about your project's goals and specifications. Include information such as the target languages for translation or dubbing, desired voice characteristics, emotional tones to capture, or specific audio processing requirements, outlining the workflow here can serve as valuable documentation for organizational purposes.

source_language.description: The language of the input text. Pass a locale tag (`en-us`, `fr-fr`, `es-es`). Numeric language IDs (`1` or `"1"`) still work but are deprecated. (see list_source_languages).

target_language.description: The target output language. Pass a locale tag (`fr-fr`, `es-es`, `de-de`). Numeric language IDs still work but are deprecated. (see list_target_languages).

texts.description: An array of strings to be translated. This field is required and can contain multiple text segments for batch translation.

age.description: An integer representing the intended audience age. This helps adjust vocabulary and expressions to be age-appropriate, which is particularly important when translating content for children, teenagers, or specific age demographics.

formality.description: Formality of the translation: 1 or 2 (CAMB.AI's translation guide lists 1 formal, 2 casual).

gender.description: Grammatical gender preference: 0 not specified, 1 male, 2 female, 9 neutral.

chosen_dictionaries.description: An optional parameter that allows you to specify specialized vocabulary dictionaries to use during translation. This ensures that technical terms are translated appropriately for specific fields like medicine, law, technology, or other industries.

output.description: The new translation task; poll its `task_id` with the matching status tool.

task_id.description: Id to poll for status.

get_translation_status.description: Check the status of a translation task. Poll until `status` is SUCCESS (keep polling while PENDING; ERROR, TIMEOUT and PAYMENT_REQUIRED are terminal), then use the returned `run_id` with get_translation_result.

task_id.description: A unique identifier for the task. This is used to query the status of the translation task that is running. It is returned when a create request is made for translation.

output.description: Task status: `status` is PENDING, SUCCESS, ERROR, TIMEOUT or PAYMENT_REQUIRED; `run_id` is set once it succeeds.

get_translation_results_bulk.title: Get translation results in bulk
get_translation_results_bulk.description: Fetch the translated texts of several translation runs at once. Takes 2 to 5 run ids of the same run type and returns their results keyed by run id.

run_ids.description: An array of unique positive integers, each representing the ID of a specific run. You must provide between 2 and 5 IDs, and all IDs must correspond to the same run type (e.g., all text-to-speech or all dubbing runs).

list_voices.title: List voices
list_voices.description: List every voice available to the API key: public, shared and custom voices, each with id, name, gender, age and language. Voice ids from here are what the TTS, dubbing, narration and stream tools take.

delete_voice.title: Delete a voice
delete_voice.description: Permanently delete a custom voice from the workspace by id. Public and shared voices cannot be deleted.

voice_id.description: The unique identifier of the custom voice to delete (see list_voices).

create_voice_from_description.title: Create voice from description
create_voice_from_description.description: Design a new voice from a written description (at least ~18 words of gender, age, accent, tone and style) and a sample text to speak. Returns a task_id; poll get_voice_from_description_status, then get_voice_from_description_result for audio previews.

text.description: The text content that will be converted into synthesized speech. This text will be spoken by your generated voice and serves as a sample of the voice's capabilities.

voice_description.description: A detailed description (minimum 18 words/100+ characters) of the desired voice characteristics. Be specific about gender, age, accent, emotional tone, speaking style, or cultural context to guide the synthesis engine in creating an authentic voice.

output.description: The new voice design task; poll its `task_id` with the matching status tool.

task_id.description: Id to poll for status.

get_voice_from_description_status.title: Get voice from description status
get_voice_from_description_status.description: Check the status of a voice-from-description task. Poll until `status` is SUCCESS (keep polling while PENDING; ERROR, TIMEOUT and PAYMENT_REQUIRED are terminal), then use the returned `run_id` with get_voice_from_description_result.

task_id.description: A unique identifier for the task. This is used to query the status of the text to voice task that is running. It is returned when a create request is made for text to voice.

output.description: Task status: `status` is PENDING, SUCCESS, ERROR, TIMEOUT or PAYMENT_REQUIRED; `run_id` is set once it succeeds.

status.description: PENDING, SUCCESS, ERROR, TIMEOUT or PAYMENT_REQUIRED.

run_id.description: The run holding the result, once status is SUCCESS.

get_voice_from_description_result.title: Get voice from description result
get_voice_from_description_result.description: Get the audio previews generated by a finished voice-from-description run, one per interpretation of the description.

run_id.description: The unique identifier for the run, which was generated during the text to voice creation process and returned upon task completion.

list_dictionaries.title: List dictionaries
list_dictionaries.description: List the pronunciation and terminology dictionaries in the workspace. Dictionary ids from here can be passed as chosen_dictionaries to translation, TTS and dubbing tools.

get_dictionary.title: Get dictionary summary
get_dictionary.description: Get a dictionary's summary (id, name, description, timestamps) without its terms. Use get_dictionary_details to read the terms.

dictionary_id.description: This parameter tells the API exactly which dictionary you're interested in. Each dictionary in the system has a unique numerical ID that serves as its primary identifier.

get_dictionary_details.title: Get dictionary details
get_dictionary_details.description: Get a dictionary with its terms and their translations, optionally limited in count or filtered by a search term. Term ids from here are what update_dictionary_term and delete_dictionary_term take.

dictionary_id.description: This parameter tells the API exactly which dictionary you're interested in. Each dictionary in the system has a unique numerical ID that serves as its primary identifier.

limit.description: Limit how many terms are returned when fetching the dictionary details. You can specify exactly how many terms you want to see. For example, setting `limit=50` will return only the first 50 terms from the dictionary. This is especially useful for implementing pagination in user interfaces or when you only need a sample of the dictionary's content.

search_term.description: When you provide a search term, the API acts like a search function within the dictionary. Rather than returning all terms, it will filter the results to show only those terms that match or contain your search string. This transforms the endpoint from a 'show me everything' request into a 'show me what I'm looking for' request, making it much more efficient when you're looking for specific terminology.

delete_dictionary.title: Delete a dictionary
delete_dictionary.description: Permanently delete a dictionary and all of its terms and translations. This cannot be undone.

dictionary_id.description: This parameter tells the API exactly which dictionary you're interested in. Each dictionary in the system has a unique numerical ID that serves as its primary identifier.

add_dictionary_term.title: Add a term to a dictionary
add_dictionary_term.description: Add a term to a dictionary as a list of translations, each a text plus its language.

dictionary_id.description: This parameter tells the API exactly which dictionary you're interested in. Each dictionary in the system has a unique numerical ID that serves as its primary identifier.

translations.description: The term's translations: objects of {translation, language}, where language is a locale tag such as fr-fr.

update_dictionary_term.title: Update a dictionary term
update_dictionary_term.description: Replace or add translations of an existing dictionary term. Find term ids with get_dictionary_details.

dictionary_id.description: This parameter tells the API exactly which dictionary you're interested in. Each dictionary in the system has a unique numerical ID that serves as its primary identifier.

term_id.description: The unique identifier of the term. This must be a positive integer that corresponds to an existing term in the system.

translations.description: Translations to set: objects of {translation, language}, where language is a locale tag such as fr-fr.

delete_dictionary_term.title: Delete a dictionary term
delete_dictionary_term.description: Permanently remove one term and all its translations from a dictionary; other terms are untouched.

dictionary_id.description: This parameter tells the API exactly which dictionary you're interested in. Each dictionary in the system has a unique numerical ID that serves as its primary identifier.

term_id.description: The unique identifier of the term. This must be a positive integer that corresponds to an existing term in the system.

list_folders.title: List folders
list_folders.description: List the folders in the CAMB.AI workspace, optionally filtered by a partial name. Folder ids can be passed as folder_id when creating subtitles, project setups and narrations.

limit.description: Control the maximum number of folder items returned in a single API response to optimize performance and manage data consumption. Set this value between 1 and 100 based on your application's needs - use smaller limits for faster initial loading and pagination scenarios, or larger limits when you need comprehensive folder overviews. This parameter helps balance API response speed with data completeness, ensuring your workspace queries remain responsive even with extensive folder collections.

search_query.description: Filter folders by entering partial or complete folder names to quickly locate specific organizational containers within your CAMB.AI workspace. The search functionality matches against folder names using case-insensitive partial matching, allowing you to find folders like 'Marketing Projects' by searching for terms like 'market' or 'proj'. This targeted filtering becomes invaluable as your workspace grows, enabling rapid navigation to relevant project folders without scrolling through extensive folder lists.

create_folder.title: Create folder
create_folder.description: Create a folder in the CAMB.AI workspace to organise projects; returns its folder_id.

folder_name.description: Display name for the folder as it appears in your CAMB.AI workspace dashboard. Choose meaningful names that reflect the folder's purpose or project category, such as 'Marketing Audio Projects' or 'Podcast Transcriptions', to help you and your team quickly identify and navigate to the right organizational container for your tasks.

list_source_languages.title: List source languages
list_source_languages.description: List every source language CAMB.AI accepts, with its numeric id, name and short locale name. Use these values for source_language and language arguments.

list_target_languages.title: List target languages
list_target_languages.description: List every target language CAMB.AI can produce, with its numeric id, name and short locale name. Use these values for target_language(s) arguments.

create_spot_transcription.title: Create spot transcription
create_spot_transcription.description: Re-transcribe a time window of an existing run without redoing the whole transcript, optionally auto-detecting the language. Returns a task_id; poll get_spot_transcription_status.

run_id.description: The run to re-transcribe. Must already have a transcript.

revision_num.description: Revision to re-transcribe. Defaults to the run's latest revision.

start_seconds.description: Start of the window to re-transcribe. Defaults to the start of the media.

end_seconds.description: End of the window to re-transcribe. Defaults to the end of the media.

source_language.description: Language spoken in the window. Defaults to the run's source language.

auto_detect_language.description: Detect the spoken language instead of supplying source_language.

revision_num.description: Revision to describe. Defaults to the run's latest revision.

create_narration.description: Narrate a video with a chosen voice, either reading a supplied script (script_file_key) or one written automatically, or describing what is on screen (narration_type=audio_description). Creates a new run; poll get_narration_status.

project_description.description: Description of the new narration project.

folder_id.description: Folder to create the run in (see list_folders).

narration_type.description: NARRATION reads a script; AUDIO_DESCRIPTION describes what is on screen.

remove_fg_audio.description: Drop the original foreground audio under the narration.

chosen_dictionaries.description: Dictionary ids applied to the narration (see list_dictionaries).

speech_model.description: Speech model used to read the narration. Same choices as the /tts-stream API (e.g. mars-pro, mars-81, mars-81-flash, mars-instruct). Omit to let the system choose automatically.

passphrase.description: Optional passphrase for authenticated streams (commonly used with SRT).

stream_id.description: Optional SRT `streamid` the source requires. This is not the Camb.ai stream ID.

create_stream.title: Create a live stream
create_stream.description: Create a live stream that ingests a source feed (pulled via source_stream, or pushed to a hosted ingest via deferred_source_stream), runs AI pipelines (demixing, transcription, translation, re-voicing) and publishes dubbed, translated or transcribed outputs to target streams between start_time and end_time. Use probe_stream first to find track selectors; list_flow_regions for regions.

name.description: Display name for the stream. Auto-generated if omitted.

initial_delay.description: Seconds of setup lead time before processing starts. Larger values give the pipeline more headroom to warm up; smaller values start output sooner.

voices.description: Optional voice IDs from `GET /list-voices` to use for dubbed speech. If provided, these fixed voices are used; if omitted or empty, voices are cloned from the speakers in the source audio. When providing voices, include different genders and tones so each speaker can be matched to the most suitable voice.

dictionaries.description: Optional dictionary IDs for custom terminology (up to 5), from `GET /dictionaries`.

start_time.description: Optional scheduled start in ISO 8601 with a UTC offset, e.g. `2026-08-01T19:30:00Z`. If omitted, the stream starts as soon as it is created. Cannot be in the past; at most 7 days in the future.

end_time.description: When the stream stops, in ISO 8601 with a UTC offset. Required; must be at least 15 minutes after the start. To end a stream earlier, delete it; to change the end, patch it.

timezone.description: IANA time zone name (e.g. `UTC`, `Europe/London`) that `start_time`/`end_time` are expressed in. Its offset must match the timestamps.

audio_selections.description: Named audio tracks of the source that pipelines process.

processing_profiles.description: Reusable AI processing configurations referenced by pipelines.

encoding_profiles.description: Optional reusable encoding configurations referenced by target inputs (encoding_policy explicit).

pipelines.description: Processing pipelines connecting audio selections to profiles and outputs.

source_stream.description: The live source to pull: {id, url, category?, passphrase?, streamid?, latency?}. Set this or deferred_source_stream, not both.

id.description: Your identifier for the source stream, e.g. `main-feed`.

url.description: URL of the live source to ingest, e.g. `srt://ingest.example.com:9000`.

category.description: Content category of the source stream, used to tune processing. | Value | Category | |---|---| | `1` | News and information | | `2` | Sports and entertainment | | `3` | Business and professional | | `

passphrase.description: SRT encryption passphrase for the source, if the source is encrypted (10-79 characters).

streamid.description: SRT `streamid` to send when connecting to the source, if it requires one. Not the Camb.ai stream ID.

latency.description: SRT receive latency in milliseconds (20-8000). Higher values tolerate more network jitter at the cost of delay. Recommended: `2000` for typical internet links.

deferred_source_stream.description: A source you push to CAMB.AI instead: {id, region?}; the ingest URL is returned as source_publish_url. Set this or source_stream, not both.

id.description: Your identifier for the source stream, e.g. `main-feed`.

region.description: Region to host the ingest in, one of `GET /flows/regions`. Defaults to `us-central1`. Fixed once the stream is created.

target_streams.description: Destinations for the processed output (at least one). Each has id, type (1 SRT caller, 2 RTMP, 3 HLS recording, 4 YouTube RTMP, 5 YouTube HLS, 6 SRT listener, 11 sidecar subtitle), url (omit for 3 and 6), inputs, passthrough_policy and optional SRT settings.

get_stream.title: Get stream status
get_stream.description: Get a stream's current status (1 scheduled, 2 setting up, 3 started, 4 ended, 5 interrupted, 6 error), source details, and the state and URLs of every output.

stream_id.description: Identifier returned when the stream was created.

update_stream.title: Update a stream
update_stream.description: Update a scheduled, setting-up or live stream: rename it, change times, voices or dictionaries, merge configuration entries by id, or apply live pipeline_patches such as turning dubbing on or off or adjusting the mix.

stream_id.description: Identifier of the stream to update.

initial_delay.description: New setup lead time in seconds.

voices.description: Replacement list of voice IDs. Empty means voices are cloned from the source speakers.

dictionaries.description: Replacement list of dictionary IDs (up to 5).

start_time.description: New scheduled start (ISO 8601 with UTC offset). Requires `timezone`.

end_time.description: New scheduled end (ISO 8601 with UTC offset). Requires `timezone`.

timezone.description: IANA time zone the updated times are expressed in.

audio_selections.description: Audio selections to add or replace (merged by `id`).

processing_profiles.description: Processing profiles to add or replace (merged by `id`).

encoding_profiles.description: Encoding profiles to add or replace (merged by id).

pipelines.description: Pipelines to add or replace (merged by `id`).

source_stream.description: Replacement source configuration: {id, url, category?, passphrase?, streamid?, latency?}.

id.description: Your identifier for the source stream, e.g. `main-feed`.

url.description: URL of the live source to ingest, e.g. `srt://ingest.example.com:9000`.

category.description: Content category of the source stream, used to tune processing. | Value | Category | |---|---| | `1` | News and information | | `2` | Sports and entertainment | | `3` | Business and professional | | `

passphrase.description: SRT encryption passphrase for the source, if the source is encrypted (10-79 characters).

streamid.description: SRT `streamid` to send when connecting to the source, if it requires one. Not the Camb.ai stream ID.

latency.description: SRT receive latency in milliseconds (20-8000). Higher values tolerate more network jitter at the cost of delay. Recommended: `2000` for typical internet links.

target_streams.description: Target streams to add or replace (merged by id).

pipeline_patches.description: Live runtime adjustments: objects of {pipeline_id, dubbing_enabled?, mixing?, avsync?}. Applied immediately and not persisted.

delete_stream.title: Delete a stream
delete_stream.description: Delete a stream: a live stream stops and its outputs are finalised, a scheduled one is cancelled. The record stays readable with get_stream, but the stream cannot be restarted.

stream_id.description: Identifier of the stream to delete.

create_stream_template.title: Create a stream template
create_stream_template.description: Save a created stream's configuration as a named template (names unique per workspace, at most 20 templates). Use get_stream_template_payload later to reuse it.

name.description: The template's name, unique within the workspace.

stream_id.description: The id of a created stream in your workspace whose configuration the template saves.

list_stream_templates.title: List stream templates
list_stream_templates.description: List the stream templates saved in the workspace, each a named snapshot of a stream's creation payload.

get_stream_template_payload.title: Use a stream template
get_stream_template_payload.description: Get a template's stream creation payload; adjust start_time and end_time and pass it to create_stream.

delete_stream_template.title: Delete a stream template
delete_stream_template.description: Delete a stream template from the workspace; the stream it was saved from is unaffected.

create_flow.title: Create an SRT flow
create_flow.description: Create a standing SRT flow usable as a stream source or target: listener mode hosts an endpoint your encoder pushes to, caller mode pulls from your upstream primary_url and re-serves it. Returns its play and push URLs.

label.description: Human-readable name for the flow. Must be unique within your team.

mode.description: `caller`: Camb.ai connects out to your SRT endpoint (`primary_url`) and re-serves it. `listener`: Camb.ai hosts an SRT endpoint that your encoder pushes to.

failover.description: Enable a second (backup) leg. Caller flows then require `backup_url`; listener flows get a backup push URL.

primary_url.description: SRT URL of your upstream (caller mode only; required there, forbidden for listeners). To dial an encrypted upstream, append its passphrase as a query parameter: `srt://host:port?passphrase=...`.

backup_url.description: SRT URL of the backup upstream. Caller mode with `failover` enabled only.

passphrase.description: Optional SRT encryption passphrase for the flow's own endpoint (10-79 characters). When set, it is embedded in the returned play/push URLs and required to connect.

region.description: Region to host the flow's SRT endpoint in, one of `GET /flows/regions`. Defaults to `us-central1`. Fixed for the life of the flow, because its URLs carry that region's address: to move a flow, create a new one.

list_flows.title: List SRT flows
list_flows.description: List all SRT flows belonging to the team, with mode, region, active state and URLs.

list_flow_regions.title: List flow regions
list_flow_regions.description: List the regions that can host flows, hosted stream ingests and SRT listener targets.

get_flow.title: Get an SRT flow
get_flow.description: Get an SRT flow, including its play and push URLs, mode, region and whether its relay is active.

update_flow.title: Update an SRT flow
update_flow.description: Rename an SRT flow or bring its relay online (active=true) or offline (active=false).

active.description: Set `true` to bring the flow's relay online, `false` to take it offline.

delete_flow.title: Delete an SRT flow
delete_flow.description: Delete an SRT flow and shut down its relay endpoint.
